newsitem.title: USA: Federated sees same-store sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Federated sees same-store sales growth.

text.p: Federated Department Stores Inc Chairman and Chief Executive James Zimmerman said Friday he expects the retailer's same-stores to increase by 2.5 percent to 4.0 percent a year for the next few years.
Last year, Federated's same-store sales, or sales at stores open a year, rose by 3.1 percent.

At a press conference with reporters after the retailer's annual meeting here, Zimmerman also said Federated will renovate three of its flagship stores at a cost of more than $150 million during the next three years.

The three stores include Macy's department store at Union Square in San Francisco, the Bloomingdale's department store on 59th Street in New York City and the Macy's store at Herald Square in New York City.
The three stores had combined sales last year of $1.2 billion, and all were profitable, Zimmerman said.
"We are dedicated to making these world-class department stores the best stores in the world," he said.

Zimmerman, 52, replaced Allen Questrom as chairman and chief executive of the department store giant on Friday. Terry Lundgren, 44, who had served as chairman of Federated merchandising, replaced Zimmerman as president. Lundgren also was named chief merchandising officer of the company.
Federated, which also owns Rich's, Lazarus and Stern's stores, expects earnings per share to grow by 15 percent a year over the next several years, Zimmerman said.

Earlier this week, Federated reported a profit of $24.1 million, or $0.12 a share, compared to a loss of $37.9 million, or $0.18 a share. The year-ago loss included costs of absorbing Broadway Stores Inc., which Federated acquired in a deal valued at $1.6 billion in 1995.
By 1999, Federated expects annual cost savings to be $100 million, Zimmerman said. The company is consolidating several distribution centers and increasing investment in technology.
